newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria to support return of Bosnian refugees.
newsitem.headline: Austria to support return of Bosnian refugees.

text.p: The Austrian government said on Tuesday it would encourage Bosnian refugees to return to their country by offering them financial incentives.

"This should not be a premium in order to get rid of them but we should support them actively so that these people can be integrated in their home country," Chancellor Viktor Klima told reporters after a weekly ministers' meeting.
The Social Democrat leader declined to elaborate on the incentives that would be offered.
The return should be entirely voluntary and Austria would seek cooperation with international aid organisations to implement the programme, he added.

Klima said the measures to be taken would be detailed by Interior Minister Karl Schloegl soon. He said he expected the European Union to contribute about 50 to 100 million schillings ($4.2 million to $8.3 million).
"We have about 11,000 Bosnian refugees and I reckon about half of them will take up the opportunity", Schloegl said.
Schoegl said between 20,000 and 25,000 schillings would be an appropriate sum but that the exact amount depended upon how much aid the EU gave.
Refugees who do not want to return to Bosnia would have to be integrated in Austria in the best possible way, he said.
